seo.desc: Crop PDF pages free: auto crop white margins with padding, or trim exact mm from each side, on all or selected pages. No upload, no sign-up.
sections: Crop PDF pages online, automatically or precisely

Crop PDF trims the edges of PDF pages. Use **Auto crop** to remove white margins around the content automatically, with a little padding so nothing feels cramped, or switch to **Manual** to cut an exact number of millimetres from the top, right, bottom and left. You can crop every page or only a range such as 2-10, and the result is a new PDF – your original file is not changed.

Cropping is ideal for reading PDFs on a phone or e-reader (wide margins waste screen space), preparing figures and diagrams for slides, removing scanner borders and black edges, cutting printer's marks from print-ready files, and tidying screenshots that were saved as PDF.
Auto crop: trim white margins

Auto crop renders each page on your device, finds the outermost non-white pixels, and sets the crop box just outside them plus the padding you choose (3 mm by default). With **Same crop box on every page** ticked, the tool uses the smallest margin found across all selected pages, so every page keeps the same size and content never jumps around when you flip pages – best for books and reports. Untick it to crop each page tightly to its own content, which suits figure collections and scanned receipts of different sizes.
Pages that are rotated in the file are left as they are in auto mode, and completely blank pages are skipped.
Manual crop in millimetres

table: Cut printer's crop marks from an A4 file with 3 mm bleed
Measure the marks; often 10–15 mm per side
Keep only the top half of a page
Bottom = half the page height (148 mm for A4)

sections: One millimetre is about 2.83 PDF points. If the margins you enter add up to more than the page width or height, you will see an error naming the page, so nothing is cropped by mistake.
How to crop a PDF for free

steps: Drop the PDF on this page.
Choose Auto crop (and padding) or Manual margins in mm.
Optionally type a page range such as 1-3,5.
Press Crop and download the cropped PDF.

sections: Is cropping permanent?

PDF cropping works by changing the page's visible area – the crop box, media box, trim box and bleed box are all set to the new size, so every viewer and printer shows the cropped page. The content outside the box is hidden, not erased, which keeps quality perfect and the operation lossless. If you need hidden content to be truly gone (for example, confidential notes in a margin), use [Redact PDF](/redact-pdf/) or [Flatten PDF](/flatten-pdf/) in *all content* mode afterwards.
Crop PDF to JPG

To get a cropped picture rather than a PDF – a figure for a presentation or a website – crop here first, then convert the result with [PDF to JPG](/pdf-to-jpg/) or [PDF to PNG](/pdf-to-png/). Because the crop box is respected, the images contain only the area you kept.
Crop vs resize

Cropping removes edges and makes the page smaller. [Resize PDF](/resize-pdf/) changes the paper size – for example, from Letter to A4 – by scaling the content to fit. If a document must be a specific paper size after cropping, crop first and then resize.
Tips for the best result

list: For books, keep *same crop box* on so pages line up; for mixed documents, turn it off.
Add 2–5 mm padding to avoid text touching the edge on e-readers.
Scanned pages with grey backgrounds or dark borders may not count as ‘white’; use manual crop or clean the scan first.
Crop only the pages that need it by entering a range – covers often have different margins.
Check the first and last page after cropping: page numbers in the footer are content too and will be kept.

sections: Crop PDF online vs desktop software

Desktop editors can crop pages, but usually require a paid licence. Most online croppers upload your file to a server. This tool gives you auto and manual cropping for free, entirely in your browser – useful for contracts, drawings and other files you would rather not upload.

seo.title: Convert PDF to Grayscale or Black & White Free
seo.desc: Convert PDF to grayscale or pure black and white with an adjustable threshold. Three quality levels. Free, no upload, no sign-up, works offline.
sections: Convert a PDF to grayscale or black and white

This tool removes colour from a PDF. **Grayscale** turns every colour into a matching shade of grey – the look of a good black-and-white photocopy, keeping photos and charts readable. **Black & white** goes further and turns every pixel pure black or pure white using a threshold you control, which gives crisp, high-contrast pages for text documents, forms and signatures, and the smallest files for scans.

Common reasons: a print shop or court filing system requires grayscale, you want to print without using colour ink, a coloured background makes a scan hard to read, or you need to shrink a colourful scanned document.
Grayscale vs black and white
If you are unsure, start with grayscale. Use black and white when the pages are mostly text and you want them to look like a clean fax or laser print.
Choosing the black & white threshold

Each pixel's brightness (0 = black, 255 = white) is compared with the threshold. The default of 160 works for most office documents. Raise it (180–200) if light or thin text disappears; lower it (120–140) if grey paper, stains or a coloured background turn into black speckles. Run it once, check the result, and adjust – it only takes seconds.
Quality levels
How to convert a PDF to grayscale

Choose Grayscale or Black & white (and threshold).
Pick a quality level.
Convert and download.

sections: What happens to text

To guarantee every colour is removed – including colours inside images, gradients, transparency and embedded graphics – each page is rendered and saved as an image. The pages look exactly like the original in grey, but text is no longer selectable or searchable. If you need searchable text, run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/) on the result, which adds an invisible text layer back. Keep your colour original for editing.
Printing in grayscale without converting

Most print dialogs have a *grayscale* or *black and white* option, which is enough for one-off printing at home. Converting the file is better when you send it to someone else, upload it to a portal that rejects colour, want consistent results on any printer, or need a smaller file.
Can a grayscale PDF be turned back into colour?
No – the colour information is removed. There is no reliable way to restore the original colours from a grey version, so always keep the colour original.

seo.title: Flatten PDF – Lock Form Fields & Annotations Free
seo.desc: Flatten PDF forms and annotations so they cannot be edited: flatten form fields only, or all content into page images. Free, no upload, no sign-up.
sections: What does it mean to flatten a PDF?

Flattening merges interactive or layered parts of a PDF – fillable form fields, check boxes, drop-downs, comments, stamps and drawings – into the page itself. The document looks the same, but those elements stop being separate editable objects. A flattened form shows the answers as ordinary page content that cannot be changed by clicking into a field, and it prints and displays the same in every viewer.

People flatten PDFs before sending completed applications, contracts or tax forms, before archiving, when a portal rejects files with form fields, and when filled-in answers disappear or look different in another app.
Two flatten modes

table: Each field's current value is drawn into the page and the field is removed
Every page is rendered and saved as an image
Maximum lock-down, mixed annotations, odd viewer issues

sections: Start with *Form fields*: it keeps the file small and text searchable. Use *All content* when annotations, layers or unusual form technology still appear editable or render differently across apps.
How to flatten a PDF for free

steps: Fill in the form first, in any PDF app or with [Fill PDF form](/fill-pdf-form/).
Drop the PDF here.
Choose Form fields or All content.
Press Flatten and download.

sections: How to flatten a PDF so it cannot be edited

After flattening, form answers can no longer be changed by typing into fields. Bear in mind that any PDF can still be modified with an editor – flattening prevents accidental and casual changes, not determined tampering. For stronger protection, add a password with editing disabled using [Protect PDF](/protect-pdf/), and for proof of integrity use a certificate-based digital signature.
Does flattening decrease quality?

*Form fields* mode does not touch the rest of the page, so quality is identical. *All content* mode renders pages at about 144 dpi with high JPEG quality, which looks sharp on screen and in normal printing, but text becomes part of an image and the file can grow for text-heavy documents. Use it when appearance matters more than size or searchability.
Flattening a large PDF

Form-field flattening is quick even for long documents. All-content mode renders every page, so a 200-page file takes longer and the output may be larger; you can run [Compress PDF](/compress-pdf/) afterwards. A progress counter shows which page is being processed.
Why answers vanish without flattening

Some viewers, mobile apps and print drivers do not display form field values correctly, especially when fields use custom fonts or scripts. The person receiving your form may see empty boxes. Flattening draws the values into the page so everyone sees the same thing.
Flatten PDF online vs desktop software

Desktop editors can flatten through print-to-PDF or preflight tools, often in paid versions. Online services usually require uploading your completed form – including personal details like ID numbers and addresses. This tool flattens on your device, for free.

Do not flatten a form that someone else still needs to fill in, or a document you will edit again. Flattening is a final step, like printing to paper: do it on a copy, just before sending or archiving.

seo.desc: Edit PDF metadata free: change title, author, subject, keywords, creator and producer, or strip all metadata for privacy. No upload, no sign-up.
sections: Edit PDF metadata online

Every PDF carries hidden document properties: a title, author, subject, keywords, the app that created it (creator), the library that wrote it (producer), and creation and modification dates. This tool shows the current values as soon as you open a file, lets you change any of them, and saves a new copy. You can also tick *Strip metadata* to blank every field and remove the XMP metadata block for privacy.

Good metadata matters more than people think. The title is what browsers, PDF viewers and search engines show instead of the file name; the author field can reveal a person's name or a company account; and keywords help document management systems find files.

How to edit PDF metadata for free

sections: Why strip metadata?

Metadata is a common source of accidental leaks: a contract sent to a client with the author set to a competitor's name, a published report whose properties reveal an employee's username, or a CV that shows the template's original owner. Stripping blanks the title, author, subject, keywords, creator and producer and removes the XMP metadata stream, which often duplicates them. It does not change the visible content – check headers, footers and comments separately, and use [Redact PDF](/redact-pdf/) for sensitive text on the pages.
Metadata and SEO

Search engines index PDFs and often use the document title from metadata as the result headline. A clear title and subject can improve how your PDF appears in search results and in browser tabs. The keywords field is ignored by major search engines but is used by many document management and library systems.
Can PDF metadata be edited?

Yes – metadata is just a set of text fields in the file, and changing them does not affect the pages. The only exceptions are PDFs that are encrypted (unlock them first with [Unlock PDF](/unlock-pdf/)) and digitally signed files, where any change, including metadata, invalidates the signature.
Edit PDF metadata online vs desktop software

Desktop PDF editors and command-line tools such as ExifTool can edit metadata, but they need installing. Most online editors upload the file. Here, the PDF is read and saved in your browser – handy on a work computer where you cannot install software, and safe for confidential files.

seo.desc: Redact PDF free: black out (or white out) text by search, e-mails, phone numbers or drawn boxes. Content is permanently removed, not hidden. No upload.
sections: Redact a PDF for free – real removal, not a black box on top

Redaction means permanently removing sensitive information – names, account numbers, addresses, signatures – before you share a document. The most common mistake is drawing black rectangles in an ordinary PDF editor: the text underneath is still there and can be copied out. This tool does real redaction. Every page that contains a redaction is rebuilt as an image with the boxes burned in, so the hidden text, its font data and any selectable layer underneath are gone. Pages without redactions are copied untouched, and document metadata is cleared.

You can redact by **searching** for words or phrases (comma-separated, e.g. *John Smith, 4111 1111*), by automatically finding **all e-mail addresses** and **phone numbers**, or by **drawing boxes** over anything – photos, signatures, stamps, handwriting – on the page preview.

sections: Black or white redaction?

Black boxes are the convention for legal and government documents because they make it obvious that something was removed. White boxes (sometimes called *white-out redaction*) blend into the page and are used when a clean look matters, for example in published examples or templates. Both remove the content equally.
Is there a way to redact text in a PDF without Adobe Pro?

Yes – that is exactly what this page does, free and in your browser. Professional suites offer the same kind of true redaction in their paid editions; free viewers and many basic editors only offer drawing shapes, which is not redaction.

Search finds real text only; for scanned pages, draw boxes or run OCR first.
Numbers formatted differently (4111-1111 vs 4111 1111) need each format listed.
Always review every page of the result before sharing.

You can, but redacting changes the document, so any digital signature becomes invalid. Redact first, then sign the final version.

Comments, form fields, attachments, bookmarks and layers can also contain personal data. Redacted pages are rebuilt without them; for the rest of the document, consider [Flatten PDF](/flatten-pdf/) and [Remove PDF metadata](/remove-pdf-metadata/).

sections: What does deskew mean?

A skewed page is one that was scanned or photographed slightly crooked – tilted by a degree or two, so lines of text slope across the page. Deskewing detects that angle and rotates the page back so text runs perfectly horizontal. Deskew PDF does this automatically for every page of a scanned document, measuring each page separately, and reports the angle it found for each one.
Straight pages are easier to read, look more professional, print better, compress smaller and – importantly – give much more accurate OCR results.
How to deskew a scanned PDF

steps: Drop the scanned PDF.
Optionally change the maximum angle to look for (default 10°).
Press Deskew.
Download the straightened PDF; the result lists the angle corrected on each page.

sections: How the angle is detected

Each page is rendered and analysed with a projection-profile method: the tool tries small rotation angles and measures how sharply the rows of dark pixels line up. Text lines produce the strongest, most regular pattern when they are perfectly horizontal, so the best-scoring angle is the skew. This works for typed documents, forms and books. Pages whose detected tilt is below 0.15° are considered straight and are copied untouched, keeping their original quality and selectable text.
Deskew vs rotate
What happens to straightened pages

Tilted pages are re-rendered at high resolution (≈144 dpi) and rotated, with white filling the corners that the rotation reveals. Because they become images, any existing text layer on those pages is not kept – run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/) afterwards to make them searchable, which will now be more accurate. Straight pages are copied without change.
Maximum angle

The default search range of ±10° covers almost every scanner and phone photo. Lower it to 3–5° for speed on long documents that are only slightly crooked; raise it (up to 20°) for badly placed photos. Pages that are mostly pictures or have little text may not have a clear line pattern and can be left as they are.
Tips for better scans

list: Align paper against the scanner glass edge.
Use the feeder guides snugly.
Photograph documents from directly above.
Scan at 200–300 dpi for text documents.
After deskewing, crop and compress to tidy up the file.

sections: Deskew PDF online vs desktop software
Deskewing is found in scanner software and paid OCR suites. Online services upload your scans – often personal documents like IDs and bank letters. Here it runs in your browser, for free.

You scanned a 10-page contract on a sheet-fed scanner and pages 3 and 7 came out tilted by a couple of degrees. Drop the PDF here: the tool measures the angle of the text lines on each page and rotates only the pages that need it. Pages already straight are left as they are. Check the preview, and if a page still looks off, rotate it manually with [Rotate PDF](/rotate-pdf/).
Tips for straighter scans

Place pages flush against the scanner glass edge, use the document feeder guides, and scan at 200–300 dpi. Good contrast helps the angle detection: avoid very light pencil or faint copies. Deskew before running OCR, as recognition is more accurate on straight lines. Very skewed pages, beyond about 10 degrees, are best rescanned. Straight pages also look more professional when shared.

sections: What is Bates numbering?

Bates numbering gives every page in a set of legal or business documents a unique, sequential identifier – for example **ABC000001**, **ABC000002**, and so on. It is used in litigation discovery, regulatory submissions, audits and large document productions so that any page can be cited and found precisely (‘see ABC004187’). The name comes from the Bates automatic numbering machine, a mechanical stamper patented in the 1890s that advanced one number with every press.

This tool stamps Bates numbers digitally on PDFs. Drop one or many files, set the prefix, starting number, number of digits, optional suffix and position, and every page is numbered in sequence – continuing from one file to the next.
Bates numbering example
If the first file has 120 pages, the second file starts at 000121 automatically. The result message shows the full range applied, e.g. *SMITH-000001 – SMITH-000534*.
How to add Bates numbers to a PDF for free

steps: Drop the PDFs in the order they should be numbered.
Enter prefix, start number, digits and optional suffix.
Choose the position (bottom right is the convention) and font size.
Press the button and download the numbered PDF or ZIP.

sections: Continuing a previous production

Productions often come in several batches. Note the last number you used (shown in the result), and next time set *Start* to the following number. Keep the same prefix and digit count so the numbering stays consistent across the whole case.
Best practice

list: Use a short, meaningful prefix – a party or case code.
Use 6–8 digits so numbers sort correctly and never run out.
Bottom right is customary; make sure it does not cover existing content, and use a smaller font if needed.
Number final versions only – redact first with [Redact PDF](/redact-pdf/), then apply Bates numbers.
Keep a log of ranges per production.

sections: Can you remove Bates numbering from a PDF?

Bates numbers added here become part of the page content, as they would with a physical stamp, so they are not a separate layer you can turn off. Keep un-numbered originals. If you must hide a number, crop or white it out, but in legal contexts altering produced documents is usually not acceptable.
Bates numbering vs page numbers

Page numbers restart in each document and describe position within it. Bates numbers are unique across an entire collection, never repeat, and identify a specific page in a production. For ordinary page numbering use [Add page numbers](/add-page-numbers/).
Bates numbering online vs desktop software

Bates stamping is usually found in paid professional PDF software and litigation-support tools. Online services require uploading privileged documents. This tool numbers files in your browser for free, without anything leaving your computer.

sections: Find and replace text in a PDF

Find and replace in PDF searches every page of a document for a word or phrase and replaces each occurrence with new text – the same thing you would do with Ctrl+H in Word, but on a finished PDF. It is ideal for fixing a misspelt name throughout a brochure, updating a year in a price list from 2025 to 2026, changing a phone number on a flyer, or swapping a placeholder like *[CLIENT]* in a template. Add extra pairs, one per line (*old => new*), to make several replacements in one pass.
Leave the *Replace* box empty to simply remove the matching text, and keep *Match case* on to avoid changing words that only look similar.
How to find and replace text in a PDF file

steps: Drop the PDF on this page.
Type the text to find and the replacement.
Optionally add more pairs, one per line, such as 2025 => 2026.
Choose Match case, press the button, and download the edited PDF. The result shows how many replacements were made.

sections: How it works – and why PDFs are different from Word

A Word document stores text as flowing paragraphs. A PDF stores the *final layout*: each piece of text is placed at exact coordinates, often split into small runs, in a font that may contain only the characters used in the document. There is no paragraph that can reflow. That is why genuine find-and-replace inside a PDF is hard and why many tools do not offer it at all.

This tool edits the page content itself. It parses each page's content stream, decodes every glyph with its font, position, size and colour, finds the matches, and **removes the original characters from the content stream** – the old text is genuinely gone, not hidden. It then writes the replacement at the same position, in the **same embedded font, size and colour** whenever that font contains all the characters you typed. If the original font is a subset that lacks a needed letter (common with embedded fonts), the closest standard font – sans, serif or mono, regular or bold – is used at the same size and colour.
What it handles well

list: Names, numbers, dates, codes and short phrases.
Replacements of similar length – *2025* → *2026*, *Ltd* → *LLC*.
Text on any background – nothing is painted over it, so coloured boxes and images stay intact.
Horizontal text in common fonts.
Many occurrences across many pages, in one pass.

sections: Limitations to know about

table: New text may overlap the following words
Keep length similar, or use [Edit PDF](/edit-pdf/) to adjust
Text split across lines or runs
Subset font lacks a letter you typed
Use letters already in the document, or accept

sections: The old text is removed from the page content, so copying, searching or extracting the edited PDF finds only the new text. Note that other copies of the document, earlier versions or metadata are not touched; for legal-grade removal of sensitive content including images, use [Redact PDF](/redact-pdf/).
Can you Ctrl+F in a PDF?

Yes – every PDF viewer, including your browser, can *find* text with Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on Mac), as long as the PDF has real text and not just scanned images. Finding is easy; *replacing* is what most viewers cannot do, because it requires changing the page content. This tool adds that missing step.
How to overtype text in a PDF

For a single change in one spot, [Edit PDF](/edit-pdf/) is often better: click the text, type over it, and adjust font, size and position by eye. Use find and replace when the same change is needed in many places, or when you want to be sure you caught every occurrence.
Replacing several terms at once
The extra pairs box accepts one replacement per line in the form *old => new*. For example:

list: *Acme Ltd => Acme LLC*

sections: Each pair is applied to every page. The main Find/Replace boxes count as the first pair. Lines without *=>* are ignored.
Getting the best match on fonts

The replacement reuses the original embedded font, size and colour whenever that font contains every character you typed – so the change is usually invisible. Embedded fonts are often *subsets* holding only the letters used in the document (sometimes as ligatures like *ti* or *fi*); if a letter is missing, the closest standard font – sans, serif or mono, regular or bold – is used at the same size and colour. The result message tells you how many replacements used the original font. Non-Latin characters are supported via an automatically loaded Unicode font.
Typical uses

list: **Price lists and menus** – update years, prices or product names.
**Brochures and flyers** – change a phone number, address or website.
**Templates** – fill placeholders like [NAME] or [DATE].
**Certificates** – correct a misspelt name before printing.
**Reports** – update a company name after a rebrand.
**Forms** – fix a typo in a label without the source file.

sections: When you have the original document

If you have the source Word, Excel or InDesign file, edit there and export a new PDF – that always gives perfect typography and reflowing text. Find and replace in PDF is for when you only have the PDF, need a quick fix, or the source file is lost. You can also convert to Word with [PDF to Word](/pdf-to-word/), use Word's own replace, and convert back with [Word to PDF](/word-to-pdf/); that works well for text documents but may change complex layouts.
Checking your result

The result tells you how many replacements were made. Open the PDF and check a few: look at line ends where a longer replacement might overlap following words, and pages with coloured backgrounds. If something looks wrong, adjust the text and run again on the original file – your source PDF is never modified. You can also [compare](/compare-pdf/) the original and edited versions to see every change side by side.
Find and replace in PDF online vs desktop editors

Professional PDF editors offer find-and-replace with true text editing, usually in paid editions. Free viewers do not offer replacement at all, and online editors generally upload your file. This tool gives you multi-pair replacement for free, in your browser, with nothing uploaded – useful for contracts, price lists and internal documents.
Is it safe for confidential documents?

Yes. The file never leaves your device, and replaced text is removed from the content stream rather than covered, so it cannot be recovered by selecting or extracting text. For removing images, signatures or whole areas, use [Redact PDF](/redact-pdf/).

sections: Worked example: updating a price list for the new year

A café has a two-page PDF menu exported years ago; the designer is gone and only the PDF remains. Prices are unchanged, but the footer says *Menu 2025* on both pages and the phone number changed. Drop the PDF, type *2025* in Find and *2026* in Replace, then add one line in the extra pairs box: *0161 496 0000 => 0161 496 0999*. Keep Match case on and press the button. The result reports, for example, *4 replacements*: two years and two phone numbers. Open the file, zoom in on the footer and you will see the new text exactly where the old one was, in the same font, size and colour – and searching the file for *2025* finds nothing.
The same approach works for a training handout that names last year's trainer, a product sheet with an old model number or a certificate template where *[NAME]* needs replacing with a real name.
Worked example: anonymising a sample document

Suppose you want to share a sample report with a supplier but replace the client name *Northwind Traders* with *Client A*. Find *Northwind Traders*, replace with *Client A*, and add a second pair for the short form, *Northwind => Client A*. Order matters: the longer phrase is listed first so it is replaced as a whole before the shorter word is searched. The original names are removed from the page content, so a search for *Northwind* in the output finds nothing. Bookmarks, metadata and images are not changed – check those, or use [Redact PDF](/redact-pdf/) for logos and signatures.

sections: Why some PDFs cannot be searched

Finding text depends on the PDF containing a text layer with a proper mapping from glyphs to characters. Scanned documents and photos converted to PDF contain only images: there is nothing to search until you run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/), which recognises the characters and adds an invisible text layer. Some PDFs created by older design or printing software embed fonts without a Unicode map, so copying text produces gibberish; search fails on those too. A quick test: open the PDF in your browser, press Ctrl+F and search for the word. If the viewer finds it, this tool will almost always find it as well.
Case sensitivity, whole words and partial matches

With *Match case* on, *Ltd* does not match *LTD* or *ltd*. Turn it off to catch every variant – but be aware that the replacement is written exactly as you typed it. The search matches text inside longer words too: replacing *cat* would also change *category* and *concatenate*. To avoid this, include surrounding characters, such as a space or punctuation (*cat.* or *cat *), or use a longer, unique phrase. When in doubt, check the replacement count against what you expect.
Keeping the layout tidy

Because PDFs do not reflow, the best results come from replacements that are about the same width as the original. Digits, dates and codes are easy. Names of different lengths need a little care: *Jo Smith → Jonathan Smithson* will run past the original space. Options are to abbreviate, to use a slightly smaller wording, or to fix that one place by hand in [Edit PDF](/edit-pdf/), where you can move and resize text boxes freely. For whole paragraphs that need rewriting, convert with [PDF to Word](/pdf-to-word/) instead.
Find and replace on a phone or tablet

The tool runs in mobile browsers, including Safari on iPhone and iPad and Chrome on Android. Typing pairs on a phone is easiest in the main boxes; for several pairs, paste a prepared list into the extra pairs box. Processing happens on the device, so very large PDFs (hundreds of pages) take longer on older phones. The download is saved to Files or Downloads and can be shared straight from there.
Privacy and how your file is processed

Many online PDF editors upload the whole document to a server, process it there and keep it for a period. Here, the PDF is opened by JavaScript in your own browser tab. Text extraction uses the open-source PDF.js library; the edited PDF is written with pdf-lib. Nothing is sent to a server, nothing is stored, and you can even disconnect from the internet after the page has loaded and the tool still works. Closing the tab clears the document from memory.
Checklist before you send an edited PDF

list: Compare the replacement count with the number of occurrences you expected.
Zoom to 200% on two or three changed spots and check alignment.
Search the output for the old text with Ctrl+F – it should no longer be found.
Print one page if the document is going to be printed.
Keep the original PDF unchanged in case you need to redo the edit.
If the document is signed, remember that any edit invalidates the digital signature.

sections: Digital signatures and form fields

Editing a digitally signed PDF changes its content, so the signature will show as invalid in viewers – which is the purpose of a signature. Make the edits before signing, or ask the signer for an updated version. Form field values are not page text and are not changed by this tool; to change them, open the form in [Fill PDF form](/fill-pdf-form/), or flatten the form first with [Flatten PDF](/flatten-pdf/) to turn field values into regular page text that can be found.

sections: Worked example: filling a certificate template

Training providers often keep a single certificate PDF with placeholders such as *[NAME]*, *[COURSE]* and *[DATE]*. To produce one certificate, enter *[NAME]* → *Priya Sharma* in the main boxes and add two pairs: *[COURSE] => First Aid at Work* and *[DATE] => 25 October 2026*. Because placeholders are written in square brackets, they never clash with ordinary words, so you can safely turn Match case off. Save the result under the participant's name and repeat for the next person, always starting from the clean template. For many certificates, keep a text file with the pairs ready to paste.
Who uses find and replace in PDF

list: **Small businesses** updating menus, price lists, catalogues and flyers without a designer.
**Administrators** correcting names, dates and reference numbers in letters and notices.
**Teachers** reusing worksheets and exam papers with a new date or class name.
**Event organisers** changing venue details or times on posters and programmes.
**Freelancers** reusing proposals and quotes for a new client.
**Job seekers** fixing a typo in a CV when the Word version is lost.

sections: Good habits for reliable replacements

Write down exactly what you want to change before you start, including variants: *Ltd*, *Ltd.*, *Limited*. Search for the most specific phrases first and the general ones last. Keep replacements in the same style as the original – if a heading is in capitals, type the replacement in capitals. Use unique placeholders in your own templates so that future replacements are effortless. And always keep the untouched original next to the edited copy; since every run starts from the file you drop, you can try again as often as you like until the result is perfect.

If the document will be edited regularly, it is worth recreating it once in an editable format – for example via [PDF to Word](/pdf-to-word/) – and exporting fresh PDFs from that source in future. Find and replace is the quick fix; a maintained source file is the long-term solution.
Understanding the result message

After processing, the tool tells you how many replacements were made across the document. If you listed several pairs, the total combines them. A count of zero means none of the search texts were found – check spelling, try Match case off, or search for a shorter fragment. A count higher than expected usually means the search text appears inside other words; make it more specific and run again on the original file. The edited PDF keeps the same page count, page size, images, links and bookmarks as the original; only the matched text areas change.
Languages and special characters

Search works with any language whose text is stored as Unicode in the PDF, including accented European languages, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic and many Asian scripts. Replacement text in non-Latin scripts is drawn using a Unicode font that loads automatically when needed. Right-to-left text and complex scripts that join letters are matched as stored in the PDF, which can differ from how they appear; if a phrase is not found, try searching for a single word. Ligatures in some fonts (for example *fi* drawn as one glyph) can also prevent matches – search for a part of the word that avoids them.
Is find and replace in PDF reliable enough for business documents?

For short, factual changes – years, prices, names, phone numbers, references – yes, provided you review the result. It changes only the matched characters and leaves the rest of the page exactly as it was, so there is no risk of the layout being rebuilt or fonts being substituted across the whole document, which can happen when converting to Word and back. For legal or regulated documents, treat the edited PDF as a new version: record what changed and, where required, have it re-approved or re-signed.

Keep this table in mind and most edits take under a minute: drop, type, check the count, download, review. If the first attempt is not perfect, adjust the search text and run again on the untouched original – nothing is lost, and nothing ever leaves your device. For recurring jobs, save your list of pairs in a text file so the same set of corrections can be pasted and applied to every new version of the document.

faq.q: Does it keep the same font?
faq.a: Yes, it reuses the embedded font, size and colour when the font contains every character; otherwise the closest standard font at the same size and colour.

faq.q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
faq.a: Run OCR first; scanned pages contain no text to find.

faq.q: Is the old text really deleted?
faq.a: Yes, it is removed from the page content, not just covered.

faq.q: Can I remove text instead of replacing it?
faq.a: Yes, leave the Replace box empty.

faq.q: Is my PDF uploaded?
faq.a: No, the edit runs in your browser.

faqKw.q: How do I replace text in a PDF with the same font?
faqKw.a: This tool removes the old text and redraws the new text with the same embedded font, size and colour whenever the font contains all the needed letters; otherwise it uses the closest standard font at the same size and colour.
